structured_output.summary: Add a pure ASGI RequestBodyLimitMiddleware, make multipart temp-file cleanup cover every interruption, then wire a max_body_size keyword into Starlette, Router, Mount and Route. An inner limit overrides the outer one by unwrapping the outer limiter's receive wrapper. The middleware and the formparsers fix are independent; the wiring depends on the middleware.

intents.rationale: New module starlette/middleware/body_limit.py does not exist yet.
Content-Length fail-fast plus byte counting is new behaviour in the middleware.
Middleware tracks whether the response has started and sends no second response, while the receive wrapper still raises.
Neither Starlette, Router, Mount nor Route has the keyword today.
Application-level middleware is added in build_middleware_stack before the user middleware. Inner Route, Mount and Router wrap their app and override the outer limit.
Cleanup currently only happens for MultiPartException and OSError, so a body-limit error mid-stream leaks temp files.
Nothing is added to starlette/__init__.py. A test asserts the package root has no new export, and the middleware is imported from its module.
New tests are required for the middleware, the wiring and the multipart cleanup.

criteria.text: With the middleware and a body over max_body_size sent with a correct Content-Length, the response is 413 text/plain 'Content Too Large' and the app endpoint is not run.
A chunked or streaming body without Content-Length that exceeds the limit gets a 413, counted from bytes actually received.
A body larger than an understated Content-Length still gets 413 once received bytes exceed the limit.
A declared Content-Length above the limit is rejected with 413 without receive() being called.
A body exactly max_body_size bytes is allowed and a body of max_body_size+1 is rejected.
A multipart upload whose total encoded body (boundaries and headers included) exceeds the limit gets 413, while a smaller one succeeds.
If the app has already sent http.response.start when the limit is crossed, the middleware sends no extra response and the app's receive call raises the body-limit error.
RequestBodyLimitMiddleware is a pure ASGI class, not a BaseHTTPMiddleware subclass, and non-http scopes pass through unchanged.
Starlette, Router, Mount and Route accept max_body_size=None, and with the default a large body is accepted unchanged.
Starlette(max_body_size=N) returns 413 for oversized bodies on its routes, including when app middleware reads the body.
max_body_size on Router, Mount and Route each enforces a 413 for requests handled by that component.
An inner Route, Mount or Router limit larger than the Starlette app limit accepts a body that exceeds the app limit.
An inner limit lower than the outer limit rejects a body the outer limit would allow.
When the stream raises any exception mid-parse after a file part has started, including a body-limit error, MultiPartParser closes every temporary file it created and re-raises.
starlette/__init__.py and starlette.middleware.__init__ have no new names, and RequestBodyLimitMiddleware imports from starlette.middleware.body_limit.

tasks.summary: Create RequestBodyLimitMiddleware in starlette/middleware/body_limit.py with tests. It wraps receive and counts bytes, uses Content-Length only as a fail-fast check, and sends a plain-text 413 only if the response has not started. The receive wrapper raises a body-limit error that stops the stream. An inner instance must replace an outer limiter, for example by storing the original receive in a private scope key and unwrapping it, so inner limits can raise or lower the outer one.

In MultiPartParser.parse, close all tracked temporary files on any interruption (for example except BaseException or a try/finally on failure) and re-raise. Add a test with a stream that raises a custom exception mid-file.

Add the max_body_size: int | None = None keyword to Starlette, Router, Mount and Route. Starlette inserts the middleware after ServerErrorMiddleware and before user middleware. Router wraps its middleware_stack core, Mount wraps its app, and Route wraps its app, each only when the value is not None. Add tests for scoping, inner raise and lower, and the default.
